./README.md:118:* It can replace many use cases served by other search tools ./README.md:119: because it contains most of their features and is generally faster. (See ./README.md:120: [the FAQ](FAQ.md#posix4ever) for more details on whether ripgrep can truly ./README.md:121: replace grep.) ./README.md:122:* Like other tools specialized to code search, ripgrep defaults to ./README.md:123: [recursive search](GUIDE.md#recursive-search) and does [automatic ./README.md:124: filtering](GUIDE.md#automatic-filtering). Namely, ripgrep won't search files ./README.md:125: ignored by your `.gitignore`/`.ignore`/`.rgignore` files, it won't search ./README.md:126: hidden files and it won't search binary files. Automatic filtering can be ./README.md:127: disabled with `rg -uuu`. ./README.md:128:* ripgrep can [search specific types of files](GUIDE.md#manual-filtering-file-types). ./README.md:129: For example, `rg -tpy foo` limits your search to Python files and `rg -Tjs ./README.md:130: foo` excludes JavaScript files from your search. ripgrep can be taught about ./README.md:131: new file types with custom matching rules. ./README.md:132:* ripgrep supports many features found in `grep`, such as showing the context ./README.md:133: of search results, searching multiple patterns, highlighting matches with ./README.md:134: color and full Unicode support. Unlike GNU grep, ripgrep stays fast while ./README.md:135: supporting Unicode (which is always on). ./README.md:136:* ripgrep has optional support for switching its regex engine to use PCRE2. ./README.md:137: Among other things, this makes it possible to use look-around and ./README.md:138: backreferences in your patterns, which are not supported in ripgrep's default ./README.md:139: regex engine. PCRE2 support can be enabled with `-P/--pcre2` (use PCRE2 ./README.md:140: always) or `--auto-hybrid-regex` (use PCRE2 only if needed). An alternative ./README.md:141: syntax is provided via the `--engine (default|pcre2|auto)` option. ./README.md:142:* ripgrep has [rudimentary support for replacements](GUIDE.md#replacements), ./README.md:143: which permit rewriting output based on what was matched. ./README.md:144:* ripgrep supports [searching files in text encodings](GUIDE.md#file-encoding) ./README.md:145: other than UTF-8, such as UTF-16, latin-1, GBK, EUC-JP, Shift_JIS and more. ./README.md:146: (Some support for automatically detecting UTF-16 is provided. Other text ./README.md:147: encodings must be specifically specified with the `-E/--encoding` flag.) ./README.md:148:* ripgrep supports searching files compressed in a common format (brotli, ./README.md:149: bzip2, gzip, lz4, lzma, xz, or zstandard) with the `-z/--search-zip` flag. ./README.md:150:* ripgrep supports ./README.md:151: [arbitrary input preprocessing filters](GUIDE.md#preprocessor) ./README.md:152: which could be PDF text extraction, less supported decompression, decrypting, ./README.md:153: automatic encoding detection and so on. ./README.md:154:* ripgrep can be configured via a ./README.md:155: [configuration file](GUIDE.md#configuration-file). ./README.md:157:In other words, use ripgrep if you like speed, filtering by default, fewer ./README.md:158:bugs and Unicode support. ./README.md:161:### Why shouldn't I use ripgrep? ./README.md:163:Despite initially not wanting to add every feature under the sun to ripgrep, ./README.md:164:over time, ripgrep has grown support for most features found in other file ./README.md:165:searching tools. This includes searching for results spanning across multiple ./README.md:166:lines, and opt-in support for PCRE2, which provides look-around and ./README.md:167:backreference support. ./README.md:169:At this point, the primary reasons not to use ripgrep probably consist of one ./README.md:170:or more of the following: ./README.md:172:* You need a portable and ubiquitous tool. While ripgrep works on Windows, ./README.md:173: macOS and Linux, it is not ubiquitous and it does not conform to any ./README.md:174: standard such as POSIX. The best tool for this job is good old grep. ./README.md:175:* There still exists some other feature (or bug) not listed in this README that ./README.md:176: you rely on that's in another tool that isn't in ripgrep. ./README.md:177:* There is a performance edge case where ripgrep doesn't do well where another ./README.md:178: tool does do well. (Please file a bug report!) ./README.md:179:* ripgrep isn't possible to install on your machine or isn't available for your ./README.md:180: platform. (Please file a bug report!) ./README.md:183:### Is it really faster than everything else? ./README.md:185:Generally, yes. A large number of benchmarks with detailed analysis for each is ./README.md:186:[available on my blog](https://blog.burntsushi.net/ripgrep/). ./README.md:188:Summarizing, ripgrep is fast because: ./README.md:190:* It is built on top of ./README.md:191: [Rust's regex engine](https://github.com/rust-lang/regex). ./README.md:192: Rust's regex engine uses finite automata, SIMD and aggressive literal ./README.md:193: optimizations to make searching very fast. (PCRE2 support can be opted into ./README.md:194: with the `-P/--pcre2` flag.) ./README.md:195:* Rust's regex library maintains performance with full Unicode support by ./README.md:196: building UTF-8 decoding directly into its deterministic finite automaton ./README.md:197: engine. ./README.md:198:* It supports searching with either memory maps or by searching incrementally ./README.md:199: with an intermediate buffer. The former is better for single files and the ./README.md:200: latter is better for large directories. ripgrep chooses the best searching ./README.md:201: strategy for you automatically. ./README.md:202:* Applies your ignore patterns in `.gitignore` files using a ./README.md:203: [`RegexSet`](https://docs.rs/regex/1/regex/struct.RegexSet.html). ./README.md:204: That means a single file path can be matched against multiple glob patterns ./README.md:205: simultaneously. ./README.md:206:* It uses a lock-free parallel recursive directory iterator, courtesy of ./README.md:207: [`crossbeam`](https://docs.rs/crossbeam) and ./README.md:208: [`ignore`](https://docs.rs/ignore). ./README.md:211:### Feature comparison ./README.md:213:Andy Lester, author of [ack](https://beyondgrep.com/), has published an ./README.md:214:excellent table comparing the features of ack, ag, git-grep, GNU grep and ./README.md:215:ripgrep: https://beyondgrep.com/feature-comparison/ ./README.md:217:Note that ripgrep has grown a few significant new features recently that ./README.md:218:are not yet present in Andy's table. This includes, but is not limited to, ./README.md:219:configuration files, passthru, support for searching compressed files, ./README.md:220:multiline search and opt-in fancy regex support via PCRE2. ./README.md:223:### Playground ./README.md:225:If you'd like to try ripgrep before installing, there's an unofficial ./README.md:226:[playground](https://codapi.org/ripgrep/) and an [interactive ./README.md:227:tutorial](https://codapi.org/try/ripgrep/). ./README.md:229:If you have any questions about these, please open an issue in the [tutorial ./README.md:230:repo](https://github.com/nalgeon/tryxinyminutes). ./README.md:233:### Installation ./README.md:235:The binary name for ripgrep is `rg`. ./README.md:237:**[Archives of precompiled binaries for ripgrep are available for Windows, ./README.md:238:macOS and Linux.](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases)** Linux and ./README.md:239:Windows binaries are static executables.
